title_en: Sun Baorong v. Yang Huanxiang and Langfang Yujing Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over capital increase of a company
ruling_gist_en: A receipt, as a written document and direct evidence of receipt and payment between the parties, has certain evidentiary effect in proving the fact of receipt and payment between the parties. However, if the content recorded in the receipt is inconsistent with the actual time and amount of receipt and payment between the parties, the receipt alone is insufficient to fully prove the actual receipt and payment. The people's court shall also consider remittance slips, negotiable instruments, and other fund settlement certificates to comprehensively determine whether the funds recorded in the receipt have actually been received or paid.

full_text_en:
Sun Baorong v. Yang Huanxiang and Langfang Yujing Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over capital increase

[Ruling Summary]

A receipt, as documentary evidence and direct evidence of payment between parties, has certain evidentiary effect in proving the fact of payment between parties. However, if there is inconsistency between the content recorded in the receipt and the actual time and amount of payment between the parties, the receipt alone is insufficient to fully prove the actual payment situation. The people's court should also combine fund settlement vouchers such as remittance slips and bills to comprehensively determine whether the funds recorded in the receipt were actually paid.

Equity transfer is the derivative acquisition of equity, while capital increase and share acquisition is the original acquisition of equity. After the parties agree to change the method of acquiring equity from equity transfer to capital increase and share acquisition, the original equity transfer contract is replaced and terminated by the subsequent capital increase contract entered into. According to the ancillary nature of the deposit contract, the deposit contract, as a subordinate contract to the original equity transfer contract, is also extinguished accordingly, and the deposit penalty rule should no longer apply.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2015) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 191

Appellant (original defendant and counterclaimant): Yang Huanxiang, female, Han ethnicity, born on September 25, 1963, residing in Langfang City, Hebei Province.

Agent ad litem: Liu Zhendong, attorney at Beijing Huatai Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Liu Yanmin, attorney at Beijing Beidou Dingming Law Firm.

Respondent (original plaintiff and counterclaim defendant): Sun Baorong, female, Han ethnicity, born on April 6, 1963, residing in Langfang City, Hebei Province.

Agent ad litem: Qiao Yu, attorney at Beijing Yihe Zhonghong Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Cheng Shigang, attorney at Beijing King & Wood Mallesons Law Firm.

Original defendant: Langfang Yujing Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room 401, 4th Floor, Rongsheng Real Estate Mansion, No. 239 Xinkai Road, Guangyang District, Langfang City, Hebei Province.

Legal representative: Liu Shan, chairman of the board.

Agent ad litem: Jiang Yong, employee of the company.

The appellant, Yang Huanxiang, appealed to this Court against the civil judgment (2014) Ji Min Er Chu Zi No. 10 rendered by the Hebei High People's Court regarding a dispute over capital increase with the respondent, Sun Baorong, and the original defendant, Langfang Yujing Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yujing Company). After the case was docketed, this Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a hearing. The appellant Yang Huanxiang and her agents ad litem Liu Zhendong and Liu Yanmin, the agent ad litem of the respondent Sun Baorong, Qiao Yu and Cheng Shigang, and the agent ad litem of the original defendant Yujing Company, Jiang Yong, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. This case has now been concluded.

Yang Huanxiang's appeal requests: 1. To set aside items 2 and 3 of the civil judgment (2014) Ji Min Er Chu Zi No. 10, as well as the allocation of litigation costs; 2. To remand the case for retrial or to find the facts, and to amend the judgment to order Yang Huanxiang to return RMB 72 million (of which Yujing Company shall return RMB 50 million); 3. To rule that the deposit of RMB 28 million shall not be returned; 4. To dismiss the respondent's other claims, and to order Sun Baorong to bear the litigation costs of the first instance and second instance, as well as the preservation fees.

The facts and reasons asserted by Yang Huanxiang in support of her appeal are: 1. The original trial proceedings were unlawful, the judgment addressed matters not pleaded, seriously infringing upon Yang Huanxiang's substantive rights, and the allocation of the burden of proof violated the rules of civil procedure. 2. The characterization and logical reasoning of the original judgment were erroneous, leading to a major error in determining the base amount of funds that should have been properly paid by Sun Baorong, which was unjust to Yang Huanxiang. The original judgment avoided the provision in the Supplementary Agreement on Investment and Share Acquisition (hereinafter referred to as the Supplementary Agreement) that Sun Baorong should pay expenses of RMB 58,381,403.52 simultaneously with the investment funds, and erroneously determined the total investment amount of RMB 165 million as RMB 106,618,596.78; it erroneously determined the amount Sun Baorong should have paid for proper performance as RMB 125 million, but mistakenly found it to be RMB 8,529,486.25. Furthermore, the judgment erroneously split the Investment and Share Acquisition Agreement and the Supplementary Agreement when calculating 80% of the investment amount, and erroneously ordered the return of double the deposit of RMB 30 million based on the deposit collected under the Letter of Intent for Equity (Land Use Rights) Transfer, even though neither the Investment and Share Acquisition Agreement nor the Supplementary Agreement contained any provision regarding the deposit; it treated the receipt issued by Yang Huanxiang on November 28, 2011 stating "a cumulative total of RMB 140 million has been received" as a settlement of past accounts and debt offsetting to confirm that the investment funds had been fully paid, but made no mention of the RMB 12 million and RMB 3.91 million that Sun Baorong remitted to Yujing Company on the day after the settlement, leading to an erroneous judgment. The judgment's characterization of the case as a capital increase, on the ground that Yujing Company was aware of the contents of the Investment and Share Acquisition Agreement, was somewhat inappropriate. 3. The original judgment found the basic facts incorrectly. The original judgment intentionally recorded the date of the transfer on June 16 as June 14, concealing Sun Baorong's 14-day delay in paying the deposit and avoiding the fact that RMB 5 million of the deposit was only paid the day after Yang Huanxiang issued the receipt. The actual deposit paid by Sun Baorong was RMB 28 million, but the original judgment erroneously found it to be RMB 30 million. The original judgment erroneously found that a consultancy fee of RMB 2 million had been paid, despite there being no basis for paying such a fee. The original judgment erroneously treated the sums of RMB 5 million paid by Sun Baorong to Yang Xueliang on June 29, 2011, RMB 6 million transferred on July 1, 2011, RMB 1 million transferred on October 19, 2011, and RMB 10 million transferred on October 20, 2011, totaling RMB 22 million, as investment funds under the Investment and Share Acquisition Agreement, without factual or legal basis. New evidence showing a cumulative receipt of RMB 40 million in consultancy fees confirms that the RMB 40 million recorded in the receipt for the cumulative receipt of RMB 140 million in investment funds was fabricated, and each item corresponds exactly. The RMB 25.91 million remitted back were intercompany transactions and should be offset; the original judgment's decision to treat them separately for resolution was erroneous. The original judgment found that Sun Baorong had offset RMB 2.09 million in other debts with a garbage removal contract totaling RMB 230,000, and changed the three-year consultancy contract with a total fee of RMB 1 million to RMB 10 million, which was inappropriate. The original judgment's finding that "Yang Huanxiang transferred the equity to another person (Yang Qiting), resulting in a change in Yujing Company's equity structure, making the purpose of the Investment and Share Acquisition Agreement impossible to achieve" contradicts the objective facts. Since Sun Baorong had not fully paid 80% of the investment funds as agreed, Yang Huanxiang, acting in good faith to perform the contract and facilitate the transaction, sent Sun Baorong the documents for equity registration, which does not violate the law. Sun Baorong refused, and sued Yang Huanxiang in court, demanding refund and termination. This was entirely Sun Baorong's fault. Sun Baorong's refusal to sign the legal documents necessary for the equity change and the malicious lawsuit were the fundamental reasons for the failure to continue the transaction. Based solely on the capital increase agreement, the investment funds remitted by Sun Baorong to Yujing Company were only RMB 50 million, which is less than 80% of the total investment amount of RMB 85,294,876.25; Sun Baorong's performance was clearly not proper.

Sun Baorong's defense: 1. The original trial procedure was lawful. Sun Baorong's claims 2 to 4 in the original trial can essentially be summarized as one: requesting Yang Huanxiang to return RMB 140 million and pay RMB 30 million under the deposit penalty rule, and that Yujing Company bear joint liability within the scope of the RMB 90.91 million it received. Therefore, the original judgment did not exceed Sun Baorong's claims. 2. Sun Baorong has paid the full investment amount on time. Sun Baorong paid a total of RMB 90.91 million (including RMB 15 million in deposit) to Yujing Company, which exceeds 80% of the total investment amount of RMB 106,618,596.75 as stipulated in the Investment and Share Acquisition Agreement; Sun Baorong paid a total of RMB 49.09 million in fees to Yang Huanxiang, which exceeds 80% of the total fee amount of RMB 58,381,403.25 as stipulated in the Supplementary Agreement. The total of the above amounts is RMB 140 million. Moreover, Yang Huanxiang also issued a receipt for the total of RMB 140 million. In summary, Sun Baorong has paid the investment amount on time and in full as agreed. 3. Yang Huanxiang's claim that Sun Baorong only paid RMB 100 million in investment funds, not RMB 140 million, has no factual or legal basis. (a) Regarding the RMB 2 million offset against the investment amount as a consultancy fee for Sun Baorong's handling of matters related to Beifang Company. Sun Baorong assisted Yang Huanxiang in resolving the dispute with Langfang Beifang Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Beifang Company), and Sun Baorong paid RMB 8 million in compensation on behalf of Yujing Company to Beifang Company, and satisfied Beifang Company's other RMB 2 million interest claim through other commercial arrangements. Yang Huanxiang agreed to offset RMB 2 million of Sun Baorong's investment amount in the form of a consultancy fee. To this end, Yang Huanxiang issued a deposit receipt to Sun Baorong, and Sun Baorong issued a receipt for receiving a consultancy fee of RMB 2 million to Yang Huanxiang. (b) Regarding the RMB 10 million offset against the investment amount as a consultancy fee. Through Sun Baorong's consultancy work, the land of Yujing Company's project was reclassified from hotel use to residential and commercial use, resulting in a land premium of RMB 450 million. For this, Yang Huanxiang agreed to pay Sun Baorong a consultancy fee of RMB 40 million, and also agreed to gradually offset the investment amount with the consultancy fee. Sun Baorong issued receipts for a total of RMB 40 million in consultancy fees. Yang Huanxiang received these receipts and submitted them as evidence in the second instance. Therefore, the RMB 40 million consultancy fee was recognized and agreed upon by Yang Huanxiang and was not "fabricated". On November 28, 2011, the parties agreed to offset RMB 10 million of the RMB 40 million consultancy fee against the investment amount. To this end, Yang Huanxiang issued a master receipt for RMB 140 million (including the said RMB 10 million consultancy fee) to Sun Baorong. (c) Regarding the RMB 2.09 million offset against the investment amount for sundry expenses. Because the project land had been idle for many years and the project site was affected by interference from villagers and control by local illegal forces, Yujing Company had been unable to use the land. In addition to building illegal structures on the site, villagers even planted crops and operated farms. Furthermore, other project development entities dumped construction debris and garbage on the site, resulting in nearly half of the project land being covered by construction waste and other garbage, causing the project to stall. To resolve the above site issues, Sun Baorong paid a large amount of sundry expenses on behalf of Yujing Company. On November 28, 2011, when Yang Huanxiang issued the receipt for RMB 140 million, she agreed to offset the sundry expenses of RMB 2.09 million advanced by Sun Baorong against the investment amount. (d) Yang Huanxiang's claim that she had returned RMB 25.91 million in investment funds to Sun Baorong is untenable. The RMB 25.91 million that Yang Huanxiang claims to have returned is in fact the repayment of loans to Sun Baorong and her affiliated companies, not the return of investment funds, and is unrelated to the investment funds in this case. Yang Huanxiang's claim contradicts the relevant evidence and defies common sense. All payments received as recorded in Yujing Company's receipts were "investment funds", but the receipt issued for the return to Liu Jianxiu explicitly states that the RMB 25.91 million was "repayment of a loan" or "repayment", indicating a different legal nature. The RMB 25.91 million was returned by Yang Huanxiang to Liu Jianxiu, not to Sun Baorong, and Liu Jianxiu confirmed that the amount was a loan repayment, unrelated to this case. In the audio evidence submitted by Yang Huanxiang herself, she acknowledged receiving RMB 125 million in investment funds from Sun Baorong, further demonstrating that Sun Baorong paid the investment amount in full and that there was no refund. Yang Huanxiang's email to Sun Baorong in March 2012 notifying her to proceed with equity registration confirms that Yang Huanxiang recognized that Sun Baorong had paid the investment amount in full. When Yang Huanxiang issued the receipt for RMB 140 million on November 28, 2011, she did not claim a deduction of RMB 25.91 million. Yang Huanxiang's assertion that the full investment amount was never fully paid, while simultaneously claiming a refund of RMB 25.91 million, is self-contradictory and clearly inconsistent with common sense. In the Settlement Agreement between Yujing Company and Sun Baorong and during the retrial of this case, Yujing Company acknowledged that it had received a total of RMB 75.91 million in investment funds from Sun Baorong, and that Yang Huanxiang had borrowed from Yujing Company to repay other debts of RMB 25.91 million. Therefore, there is no fact of returning investment funds. 4. Yang Huanxiang's actions constitute a breach of contract and she should bear liability for breach, and Yujing Company should bear the liability to return within the scope of the funds it received. Yang Huanxiang's breach of contract, which caused the contract to be unable to continue to be performed, constitutes a fundamental breach, and she should be liable for returning the investment funds and returning double the deposit: She mortgaged the land use rights of Yujing Company without Sun Baorong's consent, violating Article 3, Paragraph 2 of the Investment and Share Acquisition Agreement; Before Sun Baorong became a shareholder, the composition of Yujing Company's shareholders and equity structure underwent significant changes, violating the investment agreement; Before March 14, 2012, when Yang Huanxiang's secretary sent an email to Sun Baorong's secretary regarding equity registration, Yang Huanxiang and Yujing Company had consistently refused to process equity registration for Sun Baorong, which constituted a serious breach, and even after the email in March 2012, Yang Huanxiang and Yujing Company never processed equity registration for Sun Baorong; In August 2012, Yang Huanxiang transferred equity again and lost her controlling stake, and her remaining 35% equity was also seized by the court, making it objectively impossible to carry out the capital increase and share expansion, constituting a definite breach, ultimately rendering Sun Baorong's contractual purpose unattainable.

Sun Baorong's claims in the original court were: 1. To terminate the Letter of Intent for Equity (Land Use Rights) Transfer, the Investment and Share Acquisition Agreement, and the Supplementary Agreement between Sun Baorong and Yang Huanxiang; 2. To order Yujing Company to return the RMB 90.91 million in investment and share acquisition funds received from Sun Baorong, and for Yang Huanxiang to bear joint liability for Yujing Company's return of RMB 90.91 million; 3. To order Yang Huanxiang to return the RMB 49.09 million in fees received from Sun Baorong; 4. To order Yang Huanxiang to return double the deposit paid by Sun Baorong, totaling RMB 30 million; 5. To order Yang Huanxiang and Yujing Company to bear the litigation costs of this case.

Yang Huanxiang's counterclaims were: 1. To rule that the deposit of RMB 28 million paid by Sun Baorong shall not be returned; 2. To rule that Yang Huanxiang shall not bear interest on the returned equity transfer funds; 3. To order Sun Baorong to pay liquidated damages as agreed in the contract, specifically the loss of RMB 30 million that has actually exceeded the deposit; 4. To order Sun Baorong to bear the litigation costs.

The facts found by the original court through trial: On August 25, 2009, Yang Huanxiang (Party A, engaging party) and Sun Baorong (Party B, engaged party) entered into a Consultancy Agreement, which provided: "Party A engages Party B as a private senior consultant for the Yujing Bay (tentative name) project, for a term of three years, with fees payable annually, totaling RMB 1 million in consultancy fees."

On May 30, 2011, Yang Huanxiang, as the transferor (Party A), and Sun Baorong, as the transferee (Party B), entered into a Letter of Intent for Equity (Land Use Rights) Transfer, which provided: "After friendly negotiations, the parties have reached the following intent regarding the transfer of Party A's equity in Yujing Company to Party B: I. Yujing Company's asset status. The current status of the land parcel owned by Yujing Company: The land parcel owned by Yujing Company available for development bears parcel number 1-1-16-0500, located on the west side of Yinhe North Road and the south side of Beiwaihuan Road in Langfang City; the land area is 133,334 square meters (200 mu); the nature of the land is granted land; the land use is commercial land and urban single-family residential land; the land use term is 50 years; the planned floor area ratio is ≤1.6. II. Regarding the method of equity transfer. 1. Within 3 days after the signing of this letter of intent, Party B shall pay Party A a deposit of RMB 30 million; 2. Party A shall transfer 35% of the equity it lawfully holds in Yujing Company to Party B at a price of RMB 2 million per mu, with Party B making payments in stages according to the transfer schedule. III. Matters not covered in this letter of intent shall be resolved through negotiation between the parties. IV. This letter of intent is executed in two copies, each party holding one copy, both having equal legal effect." Yang Huanxiang and Sun Baorong signed the letter of intent.

After the signing of the Letter of Intent for Equity (Land Use Rights) Transfer, Sun Baorong remitted RMB 5 million to the receiving account of Yang Xueliang (account number 6228...0018), and remitted a total of RMB 15 million in two installments to the receiving account of Yujing Company (account number 1300...3753). On May 30, 2011, Yang Huanxiang issued a receipt to Sun Baorong, stating: "Received from Sun Baorong cash of RMB 20 million (RMB 20,000,000) as a deposit for Sun Baorong's purchase of the 35% equity held by Yang Huanxiang in Yujing Company."

On May 29, 2011, Yujing Hot Spring Hotel (Party A) and Beifang Company (Party B) entered into an Agreement, which provided: "Both parties signed a Letter of Intent for Equity (Land Use Rights) Transfer on July 8, 2010. Now, after negotiation, the parties have reached the following agreement regarding the rescission of that letter of intent: 1. Party A shall refund to Party B the deposit paid within 7 days after the signing of this agreement, totaling RMB 10 million; 2. Party A shall compensate Party B for all losses totaling RMB 8 million; 3. After the performance of the above items 1 and 2, the Letter of Intent for Equity (Land Use Rights) Transfer signed on July 8, 2010 shall be rescinded automatically; 4. The parties have no further disputes." Yang Huanxiang signed the Agreement, and Beifang Company affixed its seal. On June 14, 2011, Zheng Wen remitted RMB 8 million to Beifang Company from her card (account number 6228...9112). On September 3, 2012, Beifang Company issued a Statement, the main content of which was: "On July 8, 2010, Yujing Hot Spring Hotel (predecessor of Yujing Company) and our company signed a Letter of Intent for Equity (Land Use Rights) Transfer, stipulating that our company would first pay a deposit of RMB 10 million, and later lend RMB 10 million to Yujing Hot Spring Hotel, acquiring 51% equity of Yujing Hot Spring Hotel. On May 29, 2011, Yujing Hot Spring Hotel and our company signed an Agreement, stipulating the rescission of the Letter of Intent for Equity (Land Use Rights) Transfer, and also providing that Yujing Hot Spring Hotel would refund our company RMB 20 million and compensate our company for losses totaling RMB 8 million. With the agreement of Sun Baorong, Yujing Hot Spring Hotel, and our company, Sun Baorong paid the RMB 8 million compensation on behalf of Yujing Hot Spring Hotel, which served as a deposit for Sun Baorong's investment in Yujing Company. This amount was remitted by Sun Baorong through Zheng Wen to our company's accounting account. The compensation was fully received on June 16, 2011, has been confirmed by our company, and a receipt was issued to Yujing Hot Spring Hotel."

On June 16, 2011, Sun Baorong issued a receipt, stating: "Received from Yang Huanxiang cash of RMB 2 million (RMB 2,000,000) as an advance consultancy fee for the Yujing Hotel project." On the same day, Yang Huanxiang issued a receipt to Sun Baorong, stating: "Received from Sun Baorong cash of RMB 10 million (RMB 10,000,000) as a deposit for Sun Baorong's purchase of the 35% equity held by Yang Huanxiang in Yujing Company."

On June 29, 2011, Sun Baorong transferred RMB 5 million to Yang Xueliang's receiving account No. 6228×××××××××××××0018, and on July 1, 2011, transferred another RMB 6 million. On July 1, 2011, Yang Huanxiang issued an IOU to Sun Baorong stating: "I hereby borrow from Sun Baorong cash of RMB 11 million (RMB 11,000,000). Borrower: Yang Huanxiang." On October 19, 2011, Liu Jianxiu transferred RMB 1 million to Jiang Qiulan's account No. 6228×××××××××××××8812. On October 20, 2011, another RMB 10 million was transferred. On September 2, 2012, Liu Jianxiu issued a "Certificate" stating: "I, on October 19 and 20, 2011, made two transfers totaling RMB 11 million to Jiang Qiulan's account, acting on behalf of Sun Baorong to pay the investment capital contribution for Yujing Company." On October 21, 2011, Yang Huanxiang issued a receipt to Sun Baorong stating: "Received from Sun Baorong capital contribution payment of RMB 11 million."

On November 3, 2011, Sun Baorong (Party B) and Yang Huanxiang (Party A) signed the "Investment and Capital Contribution Agreement," stipulating: "1. Party B invests in Yujing Company (hereinafter referred to as the 'Target Company') in the form of monetary capital, with a total investment amount of RMB 106,618,596.75. Among this, the amount credited to Party B's 'Paid-in Capital - Sun Baorong' account in the Target Company is RMB 30,708,596.75, accounting for 35% of the Target Company's equity. The portion of Party B's invested funds exceeding the 'Paid-in Capital' in the Target Company, i.e., RMB 75,910,000, shall be credited to the 'Capital Reserve' account of the Target Company, and this portion of funds shall be enjoyed by all shareholders (including existing and future shareholders) of the Target Company. 2. After Party B's investment, the Target Company's paid-in capital shall increase from the original RMB 57,030,251.1 to RMB 87,738,847.85. The shareholding ratios of each shareholder shall be: Yang Huanxiang and Ma Yuling jointly hold 65%, Sun Baorong holds 35%. Ma Yuling's shares are currently held on behalf by Yang Huanxiang, and shall be transferred to Yang Huanxiang in the future. 3. Current business status of the Target Company and the rights and obligations of both parties: 1. The land parcel owned by the Target Company and its current status. 2. The right to use the above land is vested in Yujing Company. 3. Before Party B becomes a shareholder, any agreements regarding the above land parcel entered into between the original shareholders of the Target Company and any third party shall be void and have no effect on Party B, and any liabilities and expenses arising therefrom shall be borne by Party A. ... 9. Party B shall pay 80% of the total investment amount within one month from the date the Target Company obtains the updated land certificate. Party A shall handle the equity registration procedures for Party B. Within 15 days after the completion of the equity change procedures, Party B shall pay the remaining 20% of the investment amount. If Party B fails to pay the investment amount on time, Party B agrees to pay Party A liquidated damages at the rate of 3% per month on the overdue amount. 10. After obtaining approval from the administrative authority for industry and commerce and completing the equity registration, Party B shall become a shareholder of the Target Company and enjoy the rights and assume the obligations of the company in accordance with the capital contribution ratio and the articles of association. This agreement shall take effect upon signature by both parties. This agreement is made in triplicate, with each party holding one copy and one copy kept on file with the company, all having equal legal effect." Yang Huanxiang and Sun Baorong signed the agreement.

On the same day, Sun Baorong (Party B) and Yang Huanxiang (Party A) also signed a "Supplemental Agreement," stipulating: "Whereas both parties signed the 'Investment and Capital Contribution Agreement,' whereby Party B invests in Yujing Company in the form of monetary capital with a total investment amount of RMB 106,618,596.75. Among this, the amount credited to Party B's 'Paid-in Capital - Sun Baorong' account in the Target Company is RMB 30,708,596.75, accounting for 35% of the Target Company's equity; the portion of Party B's invested funds exceeding the registered capital, i.e., RMB 75,910,000, shall be credited to the 'Capital Reserve' account of the Target Company. However, taking into consideration that the original major shareholder (Party A) of the Target Company, before and after acquiring the Target Company and during the company's operation, incurred significant operating expenses and borrowing costs, and that the funds were occupied for a long time without being recorded, the parties, on a voluntary and equal basis, agree that while Party B invests RMB 106,618,596.75 in the Target Company, Party B also agrees to bear for Party A a portion of the expenses not recorded in the Target Company's accounts, amounting to RMB 58,381,403.25, and shall pay this amount to Party A in synchronization with the payment terms for Party B under the 'Investment and Capital Contribution Agreement.' ... Except for the above amount and any other agreements between the parties, Party B shall not pay any other fees to Party A or other original shareholders in connection with the capital contribution and shareholding. Matters related to the investment and capital contribution shall be detailed in the 'Investment and Capital Contribution Agreement.' The contents of this agreement shall not be stated in the 'Shareholders' Resolution' or 'Amendment to Articles of Association' for this capital increase. This agreement shall take effect upon signature by both parties." Yang Huanxiang and Sun Baorong signed the supplemental agreement.

Before and after the signing of the above agreements, on October 28, 2011, Sun Baorong remitted RMB 3 million to Yujing Company's account No. 3130×××××××××××××××9911; on November 4, 2011, he remitted RMB 5 million and RMB 17 million in two separate transfers to the same account. On November 7, 2011, Yujing Company issued a receipt to Sun Baorong stating: "Received from Sun Baorong investment funds (three installments: October 28: RMB 3 million, November 4: RMB 5 million, November 7: RMB 17 million) totaling RMB 25 million. Payer: Liu Jianxiu, Receiver: Fan Lu." On November 8, 2011, Sun Baorong remitted RMB 3.5 million, RMB 13 million, and RMB 6.5 million in three separate transfers to Yujing Company's account No. 3130×××××××××××××××9991. On November 8, 2011, Yujing Company issued a receipt to Sun Baorong stating: "Received from Sun Baorong investment funds (RMB 3.5 million, RMB 13 million, and RMB 6.5 million) totaling RMB 23 million. Payer: Liu Jianxiu, Receiver: Fan Lu." On November 28, 2011, Sun Baorong remitted RMB 12 million to Yujing Company's account No. 3130×××××××××××××××9991; on November 29, 2011, he remitted RMB 12 million and RMB 3.91 million in two separate transfers to the same account. On November 29, 2011, Yujing Company issued a receipt to Sun Baorong stating: "Received from Sun Baorong investment funds (three installments: November 28: RMB 12 million, November 29: RMB 12 million, RMB 3.91 million) totaling RMB 27.91 million. Payer: Liu Jianxiu, Receiver: Jia Min." Yujing Company affixed its financial seal on each of the three receipts. The total of the above payments amounted to RMB 75.91 million.

On November 28, 2011, Yang Huanxiang issued a receipt to Sun Baorong stating: "Received from Sun Baorong capital contribution payment of RMB 10 million. As of today, the cumulative amount received is RMB 140 million (including the amount covered by company receipts)." At trial, Sun Baorong argued that the consulting fee that Yang Huanxiang agreed to pay to Sun Baorong had changed from RMB 1 million to RMB 10 million, and after mutual offset, Yang Huanxiang acknowledged receiving this portion of Sun Baorong's capital contribution, which was included within the RMB 140 million receipt. To this end, Sun Baorong submitted to the court project planning manuals, drawings, and other materials. Yang Huanxiang argued that the "Consulting Service Agreement" stipulated a three-year consulting period and a fee of RMB 1 million. Because Sun Baorong became a shareholder, the consulting contract ended, and there was no consulting issue, let alone the consulting fee changing from RMB 1 million to RMB 10 million.

Regarding the above receipt, Sun Baorong argued that it also included other miscellaneous expenses such as garbage removal at the project site, totaling RMB 2.09 million, which were included within the final settlement receipt of RMB 140 million issued by Yang Huanxiang. To this end, Sun Baorong submitted the "Garbage Removal Contract" signed between Yujing Company and Zhang Ruiguo on December 3, 2011. Yang Huanxiang did not acknowledge this, arguing that such expenses did not exist in reality.

Yang Huanxiang did not dispute the authenticity of the receipt he issued. At trial, he stated that Sun Baorong had made bank transfers totaling RMB 125.91 million, and thereafter, Yang Huanxiang and Yujing Company returned RMB 25.91 million to Sun Baorong. He provided two receipts: 1. A receipt dated November 8, 2011, stating: "Received from Yang Huanxiang repayment of loan (three installments: RMB 10 million, RMB 9 million, RMB 4 million) totaling RMB 23 million. Payer: Fan Lu on behalf of Yang Huanxiang, Receiver: Liu Jianxiu on behalf of Sun Baorong." 2. A receipt dated November 29, 2011, stating: "Received from Yujing Company repayment of RMB 2.91 million. Payer: Jia Min, Receiver: Liu Jianxiu." Yang Huanxiang claimed that he only received RMB 100 million as capital contribution, and the remaining amounts were not actually paid by Sun Baorong. Sun Baorong did not dispute the authenticity of the two receipts, arguing that the receipts stated "repayment" or "loan repayment," not the return of investment funds. To this end, Sun Baorong submitted to the court some "Loan Approval Notices" and loan receipts from September 23, 2008, and February 26, July 31, and November 17, 2009. Yang Huanxiang also submitted "Repayment Settlement Statements" and receipts. The loan and repayment amounts, document numbers, and parties involved in the evidence provided by both parties were inconsistent. At trial, Yujing Company argued that it merely collected and returned funds on behalf of Yang Huanxiang, and the specific nature should be determined by the parties themselves.

On September 23, 2014, the Beijing Chang'an Notary Public Office issued a notarial certificate numbered (2014) Jing Chang'an Nei Jing Zheng Zi No. 20827, stating: "Dear Mr. Sun: Please find enclosed three documents related to your investment and shareholding -- the new shareholders' resolution, board resolution, articles of association and amendments (including: 1. One original articles of association of the company; 2. One amendment to the articles of association filed before the capital increase on February 5, 2012; 3. One amendment to the articles of association made for this capital increase) sent to Secretary Liu for you. Please print out the paper documents after receipt and agreement, sign them, and dispatch a representative to Yujing Company before March 18, 2012. After all shareholders sign, we will handle the registration procedures for your investment and shareholding with the Administration for Industry and Commerce."

Additionally, it was found that: Yujing Company was jointly established by Yang Huanxiang and Ma Yuling. As of February 15, 2011, the company's registered capital was RMB 57,030,251. Yang Huanxiang contributed RMB 39,920,976, holding 70%, and Ma Yuling contributed RMB 17,109,275, holding 30%. On February 5, 2012, Yujing Company's shareholders changed to Yang Huanxiang and Yang Qiting, with Yang Huanxiang contributing RMB 45,624,001 (80% shareholding) and Yang Qiting contributing RMB 11,406,250 (20% shareholding); the original shareholder Ma Yuling withdrew. On August 20, 2012, Yang Huanxiang and Yang Qiting respectively signed "Equity Transfer Agreements" with Rongsheng Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Rongsheng Company"), whereby Yang Huanxiang transferred 45% of his shares in Yujing Company to Rongsheng Company, and Yang Qiting transferred 20% of his shares in Yujing Company to Rongsheng Company. The equity structure of Yujing Company changed to Rongsheng Company holding 65% and Yang Huanxiang holding 35%. Furthermore, Yujing Company obtained the land use certificate on October 27, 2011.

At trial, Yang Huanxiang expressed willingness to rescind the "Letter of Intent for Equity (Land Use Right) Transfer," the "Investment and Capital Contribution Agreement," and the "Supplemental Agreement" entered into between him and Sun Baorong. Since Sun Baorong did not request interest on the equity transfer price, Yang Huanxiang requested to withdraw his counterclaim that "interest on the equity transfer price should not be supported." As for the losses incurred by Yang Huanxiang exceeding the deposit amount, he argued that his cooperation with Chen Shuguo and the Northern Company had been persuaded by Sun Baorong to terminate, and as a result of terminating the contracts with Chen Shuguo and the Northern Company, he paid Chen Shuguo RMB 20 million and the Northern Company RMB 8 million, causing him losses, for which he sought compensation. Sun Baorong argued that these losses were unrelated to him.

The court of first instance, upon trial, held that: Yang Huanxiang's counterclaim that "interest on the equity transfer price should not be supported" was not requested by Sun Baorong in the principal claim. Yang Huanxiang withdrew that counterclaim during the trial, and the court of first instance confirmed this.

Regarding the nature and validity of the agreements involved in this case. The "Letter of Intent for Equity (Land Use Right) Transfer" was signed between Yang Huanxiang and Sun Baorong on May 30, 2011, and the "Investment and Capital Contribution Agreement" and the "Supplemental Agreement" were signed on November 3, 2011. These three agreements were entered into sequentially and were interrelated; all were true expressions of the parties' intent. Analyzing their content, the "Letter of Intent" stipulated a deposit. Subsequently, the "Investment and Capital Contribution Agreement" included provisions for equity transfer as well as an increase in the Target Company's paid-in capital from the original RMB 57,030,251.1 to RMB 87,738,847.85. Generally, an equity transfer can establish a civil legal relationship between the transferor and the transferee through a formal legal act of entering into an equity transfer contract, defining the rights and obligations of both parties. Whether a company should increase its capital or accept investment should be decided by the company itself. The capital increase portion stipulated in the "Investment and Capital Contribution Agreement" in this case essentially exceeded the scope of the rights of the contracting parties. However, the agreement specifically noted: "This agreement is made in triplicate, with each party holding one copy and one copy kept on file with the company." Moreover, at the time of signing this agreement, Yang Huanxiang held 70% of Yujing Company's equity and was the de facto controller of the company. Although Yujing Company denied in court that the "Investment and Capital Contribution Agreement" was ever kept on file with the company, during the subsequent performance, Yujing Company accepted Sun Baorong's investment funds and issued receipts for payment on multiple occasions, clearly stating that it had received Sun Baorong's investment funds and affixing its company financial seal. This conduct indicated that Yujing Company was aware of the contents of the "Investment and Capital Contribution Agreement." Otherwise, it would not have issued investment receipts for funds of unknown origin. Yujing Company argued at trial that it was merely collecting funds on behalf of Yang Huanxiang under an oral agency arrangement. However, in an agency relationship, the entrusted matter should belong to the principal; whether a company should increase its capital falls within the company's own governance scope, not that of a shareholder like Yang Huanxiang. Therefore, the court of first instance did not accept Yujing Company's assertion. Yujing Company's knowledge of the "Investment and Capital Contribution Agreement" without objection and its actual participation in the performance of the agreement could indicate that the agreement did not violate its will or harm its rights and interests. Therefore, the content of the three agreements did not contravene mandatory provisions of laws and administrative regulations, and they should be deemed lawful and valid.

Regarding the performance of the contracts involved and the assumption of civil liability by the parties. The court of first instance held that the focus of the dispute between the parties was the specific amount of capital contribution paid by Sun Baorong to Yang Huanxiang and which party constituted a breach of contract. Analyzing the performance of the three agreements: After signing the "Letter of Intent," Sun Baorong remitted RMB 5 million to Yang Xueliang and a total of RMB 15 million in two installments to Yujing Company. Yang Huanxiang issued a receipt to Sun Baorong for a deposit of RMB 20 million. Sun Baorong entrusted Zheng Wen to remit RMB 8 million to the Northern Company. On June 16, 2011, Sun Baorong issued a receipt acknowledging receipt of RMB 2 million from Yang Huanxiang as advance consulting fees for the Yujing Hot Spring Hotel project. On the same day, Yang Huanxiang issued a receipt to Sun Baorong acknowledging receipt of a deposit of RMB 10 million. Combined with the "Agreement" signed between Yujing Hot Spring Hotel and the Northern Company and the "Explanation" issued by the Northern Company, it can be determined that Sun Baorong paid RMB 8 million in compensation on behalf of Yujing Hot Spring Hotel to the Northern Company, and that the receipt issued by Yang Huanxiang on June 16, 2011, for a deposit of RMB 10 million included RMB 2 million in consulting fees, which is objectively true.

Before and after the signing of the "Investment and Capital Contribution Agreement" and the "Supplemental Agreement," Sun Baorong made payments totaling RMB 75.91 million to Yujing Company, and Yujing Company issued receipts acknowledging receipt of investment funds. At trial, Yujing Company did not dispute the amount received.

On June 29, 2011, Sun Baorong transferred RMB 5 million to Yang Xueliang, and on July 1, 2011, he transferred another RMB 6 million. On July 1, 2011, Yang Huanxiang issued a promissory note to Sun Baorong for RMB 11 million. On October 19 and 20, 2011, Sun Baorong entrusted Liu Jianxiu to transfer RMB 1 million and RMB 10 million respectively to Jiang Qiulan. On October 21, 2011, Yang Huanxiang issued a receipt to Sun Baorong for receiving RMB 11 million as capital contribution. The above amounts are supported by bank transfer documents and corresponding receipts issued by Yang Huanxiang, and can be confirmed. On November 28, 2011, Yang Huanxiang issued a receipt to Sun Baorong stating: "Received RMB 10 million as capital contribution from Sun Baorong, total accumulated received amount is RMB 140 million (including amounts covered by company receipts)." Yang Huanxiang acknowledged the authenticity of this receipt, but stated at trial that the receipt was issued at that time for the convenience of Sun Baorong's financing, and Sun Baorong had not actually paid all the amounts. Sun Baorong submitted the "Consulting Services Agreement," "Refuse Removal Contract," project planning manual, drawings, and other materials. He argued that Yang Huanxiang agreed to increase the consulting fee payable to Sun Baorong from RMB 1 million to RMB 10 million, and this also included other miscellaneous fees such as RMB 2.09 million for project site refuse removal, and that after offsetting each other, Yang Huanxiang confirmed receipt of this portion of Sun Baorong's capital contribution, which was included in the RMB 140 million receipt. Although Yang Huanxiang denied this, he did not submit sufficient evidence to prove his denial. As a person with full capacity for civil conduct, and with many years of business experience in real estate development and operation, Yang Huanxiang possessed the ability to correctly judge commercial conduct, and he should also have been aware of the consequences of issuing the receipt for payment received. He claimed that Sun Baorong had not paid the full amount. However, within a reasonable period after issuing the receipt, he also failed to provide effective evidence to prove that he had ever demanded payment of the overdue amount from Sun Baorong, and he sent an email promising to handle the change of equity registration procedures for Sun Baorong. It is inconsistent with common sense that he later denied this until Sun Baorong filed the lawsuit. Yang Huanxiang argued that after receiving the payments, he returned RMB 25.91 million to Sun Baorong on November 8 and 29, 2011. However, the receipts he provided showed the words "repayment of loan" (huan jiekuan) and "repayment" (huan kuan), which are different in nature from the return of investment capital contributions. Among these, the RMB 23 million repaid on November 8, 2011, occurred before November 28, 2011, the date Yang Huanxiang issued the total receipt for RMB 140 million, but this RMB 23 million was not deducted from the total receipt. The RMB 291,000 repaid on November 29, 2011, although occurring the day after Yang Huanxiang issued the total receipt, was not requested by him to be deducted from the RMB 140 million total receipt within a reasonable time. This further confirms the objective authenticity of the RMB 140 million total receipt issued by Yang Huanxiang. Moreover, during the performance of the contract, especially when Yang Huanxiang believed that Sun Baorong had not yet paid the full investment amount, proactively returning the investment amount was unreasonable. Both parties submitted "Loan Approval Notices" and loan instruments for 2008 and 2009, "Repayment Settlement Statements" and receipts, but the amounts, serial numbers, and parties of the loans and repayments shown in the evidence were inconsistent. The nature of the disputed amounts in this part between the parties is not the same as the legal relationship involved in this case, and the parties may independently settle this through separate liquidation. Therefore, the court of first instance determined that the amount paid by Sun Baorong was RMB 140 million.

According to the "Equity Investment Agreement," Sun Baorong should have paid 80% of the total investment amount within one month from the date the target company, Yujing Company, obtained the amended land certificate. He performed his contractual obligations, but Yang Huanxiang failed to handle the equity change registration procedures for Sun Baorong as agreed, and transferred the equity to others instead, causing a change in the equity structure of Yujing Company, and making it impossible to achieve the purpose of the "Equity Investment Agreement" signed by the parties. His conduct constituted a fundamental breach of contract, and he should bear the civil liability of double returning the deposit of RMB 30 million. Yang Huanxiang argued that the 80% of the investment amount payable by Sun Baorong should be calculated based on the total amount specified in the "Equity Investment Agreement" and the "Supplementary Agreement," and that the deposit stipulated in the "Equity (Land Use Rights) Transfer Letter of Intent" should be deducted. His claim did not comply with the terms of the agreement itself, and the court of first instance did not support it.

Since both parties agreed to rescind the "Equity (Land Use Rights) Transfer Letter of Intent," the "Equity Investment Agreement," and the "Supplementary Agreement," the court of first instance granted the rescission. Yang Huanxiang, as a party to the contract, issued a receipt for RMB 140 million to Sun Baorong during the performance of the contract. After the rescission, he should return the amount. Yujing Company actually received RMB 90.91 million from Sun Baorong as investment funds, and should bear joint liability for repayment with Yang Huanxiang within this scope, and bear corresponding litigation costs within this scope. Yang Huanxiang's counterclaim lacked factual and legal basis, and the court of first instance dismissed it. In summary, the court of first instance, pursuant to Articles 93, 97, and 115 of the Contract Law of the PRC, rendered Civil Judgment (2014) Ji Min Er Chu Zi No. 10: 1. Rescind the "Equity (Land Use Rights) Transfer Letter of Intent" signed between Sun Baorong and Yang Huanxiang on May 30, 2011, and the "Equity Investment Agreement" and "Supplementary Agreement" signed on November 3, 2011; 2. Yang Huanxiang shall return RMB 110 million to Sun Baorong, and Langfang Yujing Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. shall bear joint liability for repayment with Yang Huanxiang within the scope of RMB 90.91 million. Yang Huanxiang shall double return the deposit of RMB 30 million to Sun Baorong. The above obligations shall be performed within ten days after the judgment takes effect; 3. Dismiss Yang Huanxiang's counterclaim. The case acceptance fee for the main action of RMB 890,200 shall be borne by Yang Huanxiang, with Langfang Yujing Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. bearing joint liability with Yang Huanxiang within the scope of RMB 577,739.8. The preservation fee of RMB 5,000 shall be borne by Yang Huanxiang. The counterclaim fee of RMB 168,075 shall be borne by Yang Huanxiang.

During the second instance of this Court, Sun Baorong submitted four "Loan Instruments" and "Loan Approval Notices" totaling RMB 12 million, showing that Yang Huanxiang and his controlled company, Langfang Development Zone Yinlida Small Loan Co., Ltd., had borrowed from Sun Baorong's controlled company, Langfang Zhongbang Small Loan Co., Ltd.; a "Receipt" for Yang Huanxiang receiving RMB 4 million in cash from Sun Baorong; a "Loan Agreement," "Receipt," and the "Civil Judgment (2012) Guang Min Chu Zi No. 1605 of Guangyang District People's Court, Langfang City, Hebei Province" for a loan of RMB 3.5 million from Yang Huanxiang to Sun Baorong on January 19, 2012; and a "Receipt" for Yujing Company receiving a loan of RMB 350,000 from Liu Jianxiu. These were used to prove that there were multiple loan relationships between Yang Huanxiang and his companies, Sun Baorong, Liu Jianxiu, and Langfang Zhongbang Small Loan Co., Ltd., and that the RMB 25.91 million returned by Yang Huanxiang and Yujing Company were loans, not investment funds. Yang Huanxiang also submitted "Repayment Settlement Statements," "Telegraphic Transfer Vouchers," "Bank Transfer Vouchers," the "Civil Judgment (2014) Guang Min Chu Zi No. 579 of Guangyang District People's Court, Langfang City, Hebei Province," and a "Settlement Agreement" to prove that the above RMB 12 million loan had been settled in 2009, the RMB 350,000 loan had been settled on November 4, 2011, and the RMB 3.5 million loan had been settled by offsetting with a RMB 3.5 million debt Sun Baorong owed to Yang Huanxiang. Neither party disputed the authenticity of the evidence submitted by the other. After cross-examination, this Court finds that the loan amounts shown in the evidence submitted by Sun Baorong total RMB 15.85 million, not RMB 25.91 million; in terms of the parties to the loan relationships and the loan dates, RMB 6 million of the RMB 15.85 million was a loan from Langfang Development Zone Yinlida Small Loan Co., Ltd. and Yang Huanxiang to Langfang Zhongbang Small Loan Co., Ltd., not a loan from Yang Huanxiang to Sun Baorong; the loan of RMB 3.5 million from Yang Huanxiang to Sun Baorong occurred on January 19, 2012, and had been separately settled; and the RMB 25.91 million was paid on November 8 and 29, 2011. The loan of RMB 350,000 between Yujing Company and Liu Jianxiu had also been settled before the payment of the RMB 25.91 million. Therefore, the evidence provided by Sun Baorong lacks relevance to his claim that the RMB 25.91 million was a loan returned by Yang Huanxiang and Yujing Company, and this Court does not recognize its probative force.

During the second instance, Yang Huanxiang provided four "Receipts" issued by Sun Baorong for receiving RMB 38 million in consulting fees, and stated that the original of another "Receipt" for RMB 2 million in consulting fees had been lost. Sun Baorong, upon cross-examination, acknowledged the authenticity of the four "Receipts." Yang Huanxiang provided a recording of a phone conversation between himself and Sun Baorong on January 6, 2012, the main content of which was Yang Huanxiang raising objections to Sun Baorong's issuance of the consulting fee receipts and requesting Sun Baorong to replace them with receipts for withdrawal of capital. Sun Baorong, upon cross-examination, did not dispute the authenticity of his voice in the recording but did not acknowledge other aspects. This Court confirms the authenticity of the above evidence, and its probative force will be specifically analyzed below.

In addition to confirming the facts found by the first instance and acknowledged by the parties, this Court also finds the following:

The "Minutes of the Mayor's Executive Meeting of Langfang Municipal People's Government" (No. 2) records: On the afternoon of January 7, 2009, Mayor Wang Aimin presided over a mayor's executive meeting, and the following matters were decided: "2. The 200 mu of comprehensive-use land acquired by Yujing Hot Spring Hotel Co., Ltd. through listing in May 2006 may be registered separately for commercial and residential uses based on the approved plan. The commercial hotel and residential projects should commence construction simultaneously..."

On December 3, 2011, Yujing Company and Zhang Ruiguo signed a "Refuse Removal Contract," Article 2 of which stipulated: "Performance period: Fifteen days, i.e., from the date of signing this contract to December 19, 2011." Article 3 stipulated: "Price and settlement method: The total price is RMB 230,000 (tax-inclusive price). Party A (Yujing Company) will pay in one installment... The balance will be paid after the last refuse removal and land leveling are completed and accepted and signed by Party A."

This Court finds that the two disputed issues in this second instance focus on: first, the amount of investment funds Yang Huanxiang should return to Sun Baorong; and second, how to apply the deposit penalty rule.

I. Regarding the amount of investment funds Yang Huanxiang should return to Sun Baorong

Sun Baorong requested the rescission of the "Equity Investment Agreement" and the "Supplementary Agreement," and Yang Huanxiang did not object. Therefore, the "Equity Investment Agreement" and the "Supplementary Agreement" are rescinded due to the mutual agreement of the parties. According to Article 97 of the Contract Law of the PRC, after the rescission of an agreement, the parties shall return the property obtained under the contract to the other party. This case is precisely in dispute over the amount of investment funds to be returned. Sun Baorong, based on the receipt issued by Yang Huanxiang stating that he had received a total of RMB 140 million, claimed that he had paid a total of RMB 140 million in investment funds, and therefore requested Yang Huanxiang to return RMB 140 million. Yang Huanxiang claimed that he actually received only RMB 100 million in investment funds, and after deducting the non-refundable deposit of RMB 28 million, he should return RMB 72 million to Sun Baorong. This Court analyzes and determines this dispute based on the evidence submitted by both parties as follows:

(1) Whether the receipt for RMB 140 million can be used to determine that Sun Baorong actually paid RMB 140 million in investment funds. As a written document and direct evidence of receipt and payment between parties, a receipt has certain probative force in proving the fact of receipt and payment between the parties. However, since the content recorded in a receipt may sometimes be inconsistent with the actual receipt and payment between the parties, a receipt alone is insufficient to fully prove the actual receipt and payment situation. Particularly in large-amount fund transactions, in addition to the receipt, other evidence such as the parties' trade practices, payment vouchers, and remittance documents should be considered to comprehensively determine whether the funds recorded in the receipt were actually paid. Specifically in this case, since Yang Huanxiang and Sun Baorong were originally friends, based on mutual personal trust, there were indeed instances in their fund transactions where a receipt was issued first and payment followed later. Therefore, the content recorded in the receipt did not completely match the actual payment situation. For example: On May 30, 2011, Yang Huanxiang issued a receipt to Sun Baorong stating: "Received RMB 20 million in cash from Sun Baorong as a deposit for Sun Baorong's purchase of Yang Huanxiang's 35% equity in Yujing Company." However, in reality, the RMB 5 million deposit stated in the receipt was not paid by Sun Baorong at the time the receipt was issued; the remittance voucher shows that Sun Baorong only remitted the RMB 5 million on May 31, 2011. On November 28, 2011, Yang Huanxiang issued a receipt to Sun Baorong stating "total accumulated received amount is RMB 140 million" as capital contribution, but two installments of Sun Baorong's capital contribution totaling RMB 15.91 million were only remitted into Yujing Company's account on November 29, 2011. Therefore, the receipt's statement "total accumulated received amount is RMB 140 million" was not accurate. In summary, this Court finds that although Yang Huanxiang issued a receipt to Sun Baorong stating a total accumulated receipt of RMB 140 million, given that the content of the receipt was not entirely accurate and the parties disputed the amount paid, the receipt alone is insufficient to determine that Sun Baorong actually paid RMB 140 million in investment funds.

(2) Whether Yang Huanxiang should return the disputed RMB 40 million in investment funds

Sun Baorong claimed that he paid a total of RMB 140 million in investment funds to Yang Huanxiang and Yujing Company, and provided vouchers for bank transfers totaling RMB 125.91 million; as for the remaining RMB 14.09 million, Sun Baorong claimed that RMB 12 million was paid by offsetting consulting fees against the deposit and investment funds, and RMB 2.09 million was paid by advancing miscellaneous fees such as refuse removal costs at the project site. Yang Huanxiang acknowledged that Sun Baorong had made bank transfers totaling RMB 125.91 million, but argued that RMB 25.91 million of that amount was merely a paper trail created to help Sun Baorong obtain financing, and that this amount had been returned to Sun Baorong, so Sun Baorong actually paid only RMB 100 million. Yang Huanxiang did not acknowledge Sun Baorong's claim that RMB 12 million was offset by consulting fees and RMB 2.09 million was paid as miscellaneous fees. It can be seen that the dispute between the parties centers on whether the RMB 40 million in investment funds was actually paid and should be returned. Based on the composition of the RMB 40 million investment fund that Sun Baorong claims was actually paid and should be returned, this Court analyzes and evaluates as follows:

Whether Sun Baorong's claim that the RMB 12 million offset by consulting fees should be supported. On August 25, 2009, Yang Huanxiang and Sun Baorong signed a "Consulting Services Agreement," agreeing that Yang Huanxiang would hire Sun Baorong as a private senior consultant for the Yujing Bay project for a term of three years, with a total consulting fee of RMB 1 million. The agreement specifically stipulated: "Any modification to this letter of intent shall be made by the parties entering into a separate supplementary contract." Under the agreement, Yang Huanxiang was only obligated to pay Sun Baorong a consulting fee of RMB 1 million. Sun Baorong claimed that a consulting fee of RMB 12 million was offset against the investment funds, but he did not provide a supplementary contract showing that the parties had amended the "Consulting Services Agreement" and increased the consulting fee. During the first instance trial, Sun Baorong claimed that Yang Huanxiang had agreed to increase the consulting fee payable to Sun Baorong from RMB 1 million to RMB 10 million. However, the consulting fee he sought to offset against investment funds was RMB 12 million. During the second instance, after Yang Huanxiang provided four receipts for consulting fees issued by Sun Baorong, Sun Baorong further claimed that due to his consulting work, the land of Yujing Company was changed from hotel-use to residential and commercial use, with a land premium of RMB 450 million, so Yang Huanxiang agreed to pay him a consulting fee of RMB 40 million. However, based on the facts found, Yujing Company had already acquired the land use right for the land involved in the case through listing as early as May 2006, and at the Langfang City Mayor's Executive Meeting on January 7, 2009, it had already been decided that the land "could be registered separately for commercial and residential uses based on the approved plan. The commercial hotel and residential projects should commence construction simultaneously." In other words, before Sun Baorong and Yang Huanxiang signed the consulting contract on August 25, 2009, the use of the land had already been approved for both commercial and residential purposes. Sun Baorong's claim that due to his consulting work, the land of Yujing Company was changed from hotel-use to residential and commercial use cannot be sustained. Therefore, Sun Baorong's statements regarding the consulting fee were inconsistent and lacked supporting evidence, so this Court finds it difficult to accept Sun Baorong's claim. Looking at the content of the consulting fee receipts, the receipt for RMB 2 million dated June 16, 2011, the receipt for RMB 8 million dated July 30, 2011, and the receipt for RMB 10 million dated August 25, 2011, all state that Sun Baorong received consulting fees paid in cash by Yang Huanxiang. This is inconsistent with Sun Baorong's claim that consulting fees were offset against investment funds, and Sun Baorong also admitted that Yang Huanxiang had never paid consulting fees in cash. Therefore, the content recorded in the consulting fee receipts does not correspond with the objective facts. The RMB 40 million consulting fee receipt was issued unilaterally by Sun Baorong, and the RMB 40 million was not actually paid. It cannot be used to prove that Yang Huanxiang agreed to pay Sun Baorong a consulting fee of RMB 40 million. The phone recording shows that Yang Huanxiang did not agree to use the consulting fee receipts as evidence of capital contribution payment, and he also raised objections to Sun Baorong's issuance of the consulting fee receipts. Therefore, in the absence of evidence that Yang Huanxiang agreed to amend the consulting fee and that the parties had reached an agreement to offset RMB 12 million in consulting fees against investment funds, Sun Baorong's claim that he paid RMB 12 million in investment funds by offsetting consulting fees lacks sufficient evidence, and this Court does not support it.

Whether the RMB 25.91 million returned by Yang Huanxiang and Yujing Company constitutes a loan or investment funds. When Yang Huanxiang and Yujing Company paid RMB 25.91 million to Sun Baorong's side, the bank payment voucher did not indicate the purpose of the funds. Although the receipts issued by Liu Jianxiu stated "repayment of loan" and "repayment," this was only a unilateral representation of the receiving party. Where the parties dispute the purpose of the repayment, according to the allocation of the burden of proof, Sun Baorong should bear the burden of proving that the RMB 25.91 million returned by Yang Huanxiang was a loan rather than investment funds, and should further prove the existence of a RMB 25.91 million loan relationship between himself and Yang Huanxiang, and between Yujing Company and Liu Jianxiu. Sun Baorong provided evidence of loan relationships between himself and his controlled company, Langfang Zhongbang Small Loan Co., Ltd., and Yang Huanxiang and his controlled company, but this evidence lacks relevance to the purpose of proof claimed by Sun Baorong and is insufficient to prove that a RMB 25.91 million loan relationship existed between Sun Baorong and Yang Huanxiang, and between Yujing Company and Liu Jianxiu prior to the payment. Sun Baorong should bear the adverse consequences of failure to prove. Therefore, this Court does not recognize Sun Baorong's claim that the RMB 25.91 million returned by Yang Huanxiang was a loan rather than investment funds.

Regarding the issue of miscellaneous fees such as the 2.09 million yuan garbage removal and transportation fee. Sun Baorong claimed that he paid miscellaneous fees, including the garbage removal and transportation fee for the project construction site, totaling 2.09 million yuan on behalf of Yang Huanxiang, and that this amount was included within the total receipt of 140 million yuan issued by Yang Huanxiang upon the final settlement, and submitted the "Garbage Removal and Transportation Contract" as proof. This Court is of the opinion that the "Garbage Removal and Transportation Contract" submitted by Sun Baorong cannot prove his claim. From a temporal perspective, Yang Huanxiang issued the total receipt of 140 million yuan for the final settlement on November 28, 2011, whereas the "Garbage Removal and Transportation Contract" was not signed until December 3, 2011, and the contractually stipulated payment time was after the completion of garbage removal and transportation. Therefore, when Yang Huanxiang issued the total receipt of 140 million yuan for the final settlement, the garbage removal and transportation contract had not yet been concluded, and there was no issue of needing to advance payment. From the perspective of the amount, the contract amount stipulated in the "Garbage Removal and Transportation Contract" is only 230,000 yuan, far less than the advance payment amount claimed by Sun Baorong. Moreover, Sun Baorong did not provide any payment vouchers and could not prove that he actually advanced 2.09 million yuan in miscellaneous fees. Therefore, Sun Baorong's claim that he advanced 2.09 million yuan in miscellaneous fees such as garbage removal and transportation fees and offset them as investment funds lacks evidence, and this Court does not recognize it.

In summary, this Court is of the opinion that, based on the existing evidence, it cannot be proven that Sun Baorong paid 140 million yuan in investment funds, but can only prove that Sun Baorong paid 125.91 million yuan. After deducting the 25.91 million yuan already returned, this Court determines that the principal of the investment funds actually paid by Sun Baorong is 100 million yuan.

The investment funds were paid by Sun Baorong to perform the "Investment and Share Subscription Agreement." After the rescission of the "Investment and Share Subscription Agreement," the counterparty to the agreement shall return the collected investment funds to Sun Baorong. From a content perspective, the "Investment and Share Subscription Agreement" involved matters such as the capital increase of Yujing Company and Yujing Company's consent to Sun Baorong's capital contribution to acquire shares, which should have been negotiated and concluded between Yujing Company and Sun Baorong. Although Yang Huanxiang was at that time the controlling shareholder holding 70% of the shares of Yujing Company, he was not the legal representative of Yujing Company, and there is no evidence proving that Yujing Company authorized Yang Huanxiang to conclude the "Investment and Share Subscription Agreement" externally. Therefore, Yang Huanxiang's act of concluding the "Investment and Share Subscription Agreement" should be regarded as unauthorized representation. After Yujing Company became aware that Yang Huanxiang had signed the "Investment and Share Subscription Agreement" with Sun Baorong without authorization, it did not deny it; on the contrary, it repeatedly accepted the investment funds paid by Sun Baorong and issued receipts. Such proactive conduct of Yujing Company should be deemed as ratification of Yang Huanxiang's unauthorized representation. Therefore, the legal consequences of Yang Huanxiang's actions shall be borne by Yujing Company. After the rescission of the "Investment and Share Subscription Agreement," Yujing Company, as the counterparty to the contract, shall return the investment funds paid by Sun Baorong. In the original trial, Sun Baorong's claim that Yujing Company should return 90.91 million yuan of investment funds did not exceed the total amount he was entitled to demand a return, and the original trial court's support for this was not improper. Yang Huanxiang voluntarily assumed the obligation to return the investment funds during the litigation, which constitutes an assumption of debt, and Sun Baorong did not object to this. Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, after the rescission of the agreement, Yang Huanxiang shall return 100 million yuan of investment funds to Sun Baorong, and Yujing Company shall bear joint return liability with Yang Huanxiang within the scope of 90.91 million yuan. Since Sun Baorong did not claim interest for the return, this Court does not address this issue, and the parties may resolve it separately.

II. Regarding how the deposit penalty rule shall apply

Yang Huanxiang appealed, claiming that Sun Baorong failed to perform the obligation of "paying 80% of the total investment funds within one month from the date the target company obtains the updated land use certificate," constituting a breach of contract. According to the deposit penalty rule, the 28 million yuan deposit paid by Sun Baorong should not be returned. The original trial court's determination that Yang Huanxiang was in breach and its judgment ordering the return of double the deposit of 30 million yuan were improper and should be reversed. Sun Baorong argued that Yang Huanxiang, without Sun Baorong's consent, mortgaged the land use right of Yujing Company, changed the shareholding structure of Yujing Company, refused to handle equity registration for Sun Baorong, and allowed the equity to be seized by the court, thereby violating the investment and share subscription agreement, rendering the contract impossible to continue performing, and should bear the responsibility of returning double the deposit. The original trial judgment finding Yang Huanxiang in breach and applying the deposit penalty rule was not improper. The focus of the dispute between the parties on this issue is how the deposit penalty rule shall apply, i.e., who bears the deposit liability.

The application of the deposit penalty rule is premised on the existence of the deposit security. If the deposit security has not been established, there is no issue of applying the deposit penalty rule due to breach of contract. In this case, Yang Huanxiang and Sun Baorong signed the "Letter of Intent for Equity (Land Use Right) Transfer" on May 30, 2011, agreeing that Yang Huanxiang would transfer 35% of the equity of Yujing Company to Sun Baorong, and Sun Baorong would pay a deposit of 30 million yuan to Yang Huanxiang. This deposit clause is an ancillary contract to the "Letter of Intent for Equity (Land Use Right) Transfer," aimed at ensuring the performance of the letter of intent. In terms of type, it is a deposit for breach of contract, possessing the characteristics of security and subordination. On November 3, 2011, Yang Huanxiang and Sun Baorong signed the "Investment and Share Subscription Agreement," agreeing that Sun Baorong would obtain 35% of the equity of Yujing Company through capital increase and share subscription. As two methods of acquiring equity, equity transfer and capital increase for share subscription are fundamentally different. Equity transfer is a derivative acquisition of equity; capital increase for share subscription is an original acquisition of equity by contributing capital to the company and subscribing to the increased registered capital, thereby becoming a shareholder. After Yang Huanxiang and Sun Baorong signed the "Investment and Share Subscription Agreement," the method by which Sun Baorong obtained 35% equity in Yujing Company changed from the previous equity transfer to capital increase for share subscription, and the "Letter of Intent for Equity (Land Use Right) Transfer" was replaced by the "Investment and Share Subscription Agreement" and therefore extinguished. According to the subordinate nature of the deposit, after the extinction of the "Letter of Intent for Equity (Land Use Right) Transfer," the aforementioned deposit contract was correspondingly extinguished, and Sun Baorong had the right to demand that Yang Huanxiang return the deposit already paid. However, in this case, Sun Baorong did not demand the return of the deposit from Yang Huanxiang but instead included it as part of the total payment calculation for the investment funds under the "Investment and Share Subscription Agreement." Yang Huanxiang also treated it in the same manner. Therefore, the parties reached a consensus to offset the previous deposit as the investment funds under the "Investment and Share Subscription Agreement." Article 90 of the Security Law of the PRC provides: "A deposit shall be agreed upon in writing." The "Investment and Share Subscription Agreement" did not stipulate a deposit security, and Yang Huanxiang and Sun Baorong did not enter into a separate written deposit contract. Moreover, Sun Baorong did not pay any deposit to Yang Huanxiang, apart from the investment funds, to secure the performance of the "Investment and Share Subscription Agreement." Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that Sun Baorong and Yang Huanxiang did not attach a deposit security contract to the "Investment and Share Subscription Agreement." In this case, there is no premise for applying the deposit penalty rule due to a party's breach of the "Investment and Share Subscription Agreement." Hence, Yang Huanxiang's appeal claim that the 28 million yuan deposit should not be returned because Sun Baorong breached the "Investment and Share Subscription Agreement" is not supported by this Court; the original trial judgment ordering Yang Huanxiang to return double the deposit was also improper, and this Court corrects it.

In summary, this Court is of the opinion that the original trial judgment had unclear findings of fact and erroneous application of law, and some of Yang Huanxiang's appeal claims are established. Pursuant to Article 97 of the Contract Law of the PRC, Article 90 of the Security Law of the PRC, and Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, this Court hereby renders the following judgment:

1. Affirm Item 1 and Item 3 of the Civil Judgment (2014) Ji Min Er Chu Zi No. 10 of the Hebei High People's Court;

2. Amend Item 2 of the Civil Judgment (2014) Ji Min Er Chu Zi No. 10 of the Hebei High People's Court to read: "Yang Huanxiang shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, return RMB 100 million to Sun Baorong, and Langfang Yujing Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. shall bear joint return liability with Yang Huanxiang within the scope of 90.91 million yuan."

3. Dismiss Sun Baorong's other claims.

If a party fails to perform the monetary payment obligation within the period specified by this judgment, interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance shall be paid at double the rate, pursuant to Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC.

Court acceptance fee for the first-instance principal claim: 890,200 yuan, to be borne by Sun Baorong in the amount of 366,553 yuan, and jointly by Yang Huanxiang and Langfang Yujing Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. in the amount of 523,647 yuan. Preservation fee of 5,000 yuan to be borne by Yang Huanxiang. Counterclaim fee of 168,075 yuan to be borne by Yang Huanxiang.

Court acceptance fee for the second instance: 890,200 yuan, to be borne by Sun Baorong in the amount of 596,434 yuan, and by Yang Huanxiang in the amount of 293,766 yuan.

This judgment is final.
